s: Voted Rotterdam's prettiest building, by public vote
w: Named for the poet Rumi and built in 2001 to serve Rotterdam's Turkish-Dutch community, this twin-minaret mosque in the northwest of the city pulled off an unlikely feat in 2006: a public vote crowned it the most attractive building in Rotterdam, mosque or otherwise.
_facts: Mosque in northwestern Rotterdam serving mainly Turkish-Dutch Muslims
Named after the poet Rumi (Mevlana), built in 2001, has two minarets
Voted Rotterdam's most attractive building in 2006

s: Rotterdam's art hall, mounting shows since 1992
w: An art space in the heart of Rotterdam that has been staging exhibitions since it opened its doors in 1992, with no permanent collection of its own, just a rotating cast of shows under one roof. Its name, plainly enough, just means Art Hall.
_facts: Art space in Rotterdam, opened in 1992

s: The pocket of Rotterdam the 1940 bombing missed
w: Built in 1389 as Delft's own harbour, a way to dodge Rotterdam's tolls, Delfshaven outgrew its purpose and became a town in its own right, launching the Pilgrim Fathers toward America aboard the Speedwell in 1620. It escaped the bombing that flattened Rotterdam, so its small historic centre still stands largely intact.
_facts: Borough of Rotterdam on the right bank of the Nieuwe Maas, separate municipality until 1886
Harbour created in 1389 to serve Delft and avoid Rotterdam's tolls
The Pilgrim Fathers left Delfshaven aboard the Speedwell on 1 August 1620; its Oude Kerk is known as the Pilgrim Fathers Church
Escaped the bombing of Rotterdam in 1940; small historic centre carefully preserved

s: Four canals born from a medieval turf war
w: Not one waterway but four: the Delftse, Delfshavense, Rotterdamse and Schiedamse Schie all share the name, a legacy of medieval Delft, Rotterdam and Schiedam each digging their own route rather than pay one another's tolls. Centuries of small-town rivalry, still traceable on the map today.
_facts: Name for four waterways around Overschie: Delftse, Delfshavense, Rotterdamse and Schiedamse Schie
Their existence is the result of medieval rivalry among Delft, Rotterdam and Schiedam over toll rights
